question:
When finding the sum

\[\dfrac12 + \dfrac13 + \dfrac14 + \dfrac15 + \dfrac16 + \dfrac17,\]

what is the least common denominator used?
solution:
The least common denominator is the smallest positive whole number divisible by every denominator: \(2,3,4,5,6,7\).

Divisibility by \(4=2\cdot2\) requires two factors of \(2\). We also need factors of \(3\), \(5\), and \(7\). Thus every common denominator must be a multiple of
\[2\cdot2\cdot3\cdot5\cdot7=420.\]
This product is divisible by \(2\) and by \(6=2\cdot3\) as well, so it satisfies every requirement. The least common denominator is \(420\), choice C.
